payload.claim: The `elif commits == 0:` branch (only reached when `cut_off_at_turn_ceiling(implemented)` is false) logs "IMPLEMENT: finished and produced nothing" for *any* zero-commit outcome that isn't a `max_turns` cutoff — but `cut_off_at_turn_ceiling` only recognizes `terminal_reason == "max_turns"` (session.py:283). An idle-bound kill, a wall-clock kill, a no-result-event crash (`_failed_turn`'s fallback sets `terminal_reason=None`), or a rate-limit/api_error subtype all fall through to this same branch and get the identical "finished and produced nothing" message, even though the turn did not finish and the agent never decided anything. This is exactly the ambiguity the spec says it exists to stop collapsing (criterion 7: distinguish cut-off-and-not from finished-with-nothing), yet a third real case — crashed, not cut off, not finished — is silently mislabeled as the latter, which would mislead an operator scanning watch lines about whether a retry is warranted.
